**Finding submitted: deviation (LICENSE — licence grant scope).**

What I found in Section 2 (Grant of Rights):
- **Revocability/term — compliant:** 2.1 hosting licence is "perpetual and irrevocable"; 2.2 internal use licence is "royalty-free, fully paid up, perpetual". No vendor right to revoke at will.
- **Successor transfer — compliant:** the grants are "nontransferable (except in accordance with Section 14.1)", and 14.1 permits assignment on a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets without consent — this satisfies the fallback's transfer element.
- **Affiliates — fails the fallback:** the word "Affiliate" appears nowhere in the agreement, and 2.2 is confined to "Corio's internal business operations". There is no affiliate coverage and no notice-based path to add them, which is a material failure of the fallback position.
- **Contractors — only indirect:** supported obliquely by 14.8 (subcontracting) and the "Corio Servers" definition ("owned or operated by or for Corio"), so I made it express in the same edit rather than raising it separately.

Redline (validated ok:true, preferred level):
1. New definition 1.6.5 "AFFILIATE" (>50% voting control test).
2. 2.1 — grant runs to "Corio, its Affiliates and contractors acting on Corio's behalf".
3. 2.2 — same grantee extension, and internal use scope broadened to "the internal business operations of Corio and its Affiliates".

The downstream licences (2.3–2.5) flow from these grants, so no further edits were needed. The comment offers affiliate coverage on written notice as the fallback if Commerce One resists.
